subject: No-adaptive-training attestation + subprocessor onshore routing (HelioHealth)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: HelioHealth Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>, HelioHealth Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial: No-adaptive-training attestation + subprocessor routing

Hi Andrew / Legal team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, HelioHealth asked Redwood for two items before final procurement:

1) A contractual commitment that HelioHealth customer interactions will not be used for model improvement or adaptive training (no-adaptive-training).
2) Operational evidence that EU customer data can be routed onshore/on-region for storage and any required subprocessors (KMS, logging) are compliant with EU residency requirements.

Attached is a proposal PDF with the no-training clause language we typically provide and a short summary of our subprocessors. To move this forward quickly, can you confirm the exact evidence you need for procurement (attestation alone vs. signed DPA amendment vs. live ops proof)?

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood signs a short attestation + we provide subprocessor inventory and an ops plan for onshore routing
- If HelioHealth needs stronger guarantees, we can do a limited-scope SOC-style attestation for the relevant subprocessors (timeline ~3 weeks)

Let us know which option you'd prefer and any procurement/legal redlines.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-no-train-proposal.pdf
From: HelioHealth Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, HelioHealth Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: No-adaptive-training attestation + subprocessor routing

Hi Marcus,

Appreciate the fast follow-up. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement:

- For the no-adaptive-training commitment, is Redwood able to accept a carve-out-free clause (i.e., no internal use for training, no derivative model updates using customer interactions)? If not, what limits would apply?
- For subprocessors, can you provide: (a) a current inventory with country of operation, (b) whether each subprocessor stores logs/outputs, and (c) whether KMS keys can be restricted to EU-only HSMs?

Procurement will likely request a signed attestation plus evidence artifacts (screenshots or a short ops runbook) showing onshore routing is enforced. Can you provide a tentative timeline for those artifacts?

Thanks,
Andrew Su
General Counsel, HelioHealth

Andrew —

Quick internal note (cc'd Kimberly, Marissa, David for ops/legal input):

- Redwood can accept a carve-out-free no-adaptive-training clause for HelioHealth usage with the following operational conditions:
  * We will mark HelioHealth customer interactions as "no-learn" at the request header and enforce at routing layer.
  * Logs that contain prompt/response artifacts are retained for 90 days by default; we can offer reduced retention for this account and segregated S3 buckets in-region.
  * Subprocessors that perform model inference (inference GPUs, KV stores) will be limited to our Dedicated EU pool where requested.

- Evidence we can provide within 5 business days:
  1) Subprocessor inventory CSV (country + roles)
  2) Ops runbook screenshots showing routing policy for tenant onshore routing
  3) Signed short-form attestation PDF for no-adaptive-training

If procurement needs signed DocuSign flow, we'll accept that; we just need a target DocuSign template from HelioHealth. Kimberly — can your team produce the inventory + runbook screenshots by EOD Monday? Marissa — legal to review the short attestation language attached.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the artifacts and the attestation draft. Procurement reviewed the ops playbook and the subprocessor CSV; we have two asks before we can route for signature: 

1) HelioHealth requires the signed short-form attestation to be delivered via DocuSign with an explicit field confirming KMS keys will be EU-bound for our tenant. Please send the DocuSign template we should expect.
2) For subprocessors marked as "monitoring/tooling" that cannot be physical-only, we need an onshore-access attestation (proof that logs containing customer prompts/responses are stored and processed in-region). Screenshots of bucket policies + a short statement from the KMS subprocessor is sufficient.

If you can provide both items by EOD Thursday (2026-10-29), procurement will approve immediate signature and then proceed to finalize the commercial order. We've attached a quick DocuSign request PDF for reference.

Best,
Jill Moreno
Head of Procurement, HelioHealth
